new_parts.name: bracket-R

new_parts.position: a second elbow bracket, free-standing -- the right corner post

new_parts.name: peg-black-B

new_parts.position: its axle end pushed into bracket-R's cross hole

new_parts.name: fork-R
new_parts.catalog_name: Technic Axle and Pin Connector Perpendicular Double
new_parts.position: set next to bracket-R, not yet joined to anything -- it has no peg of its own

what_each_new_part_touches: peg-black-B's axle end goes into bracket-R's cross hole
where_everything_is_after: bracket-R: free-standing, the right corner post, now carrying peg-black-B
fork-R: sitting with bracket-R but not yet attached to anything

why.problem_solved: Starts the right corner post, mirroring the left one from step 1 so the beam in step 3 has a matching peg to land on at both ends.
why.why_these_parts: A friction peg with a stop on both ends bridges the elbow bracket's cross hole now and the beam's round hole in step 3, same trick as pin-blue-A on the left.
why.sets_up_for_later: peg-black-B's free pin end takes the 7-hole beam in step 3. fork-R's holes take the long shaft's gray gear and right-hand bearing in step 7.
why.design_pattern: peg-in-elbow corner mount, bearing block added alongside

review_note: Item 1 in this step's parts box is read as 43093 (axle pin, friction, both ends are stops) rather than a hub-style part, because nothing else in the box has a stop to offer fork-R or the beam later -- a hub-with-one-hole part would leave this corner with no free peg for step 3. fork-R (32291) is hole-only in the catalog with no pin or axle stop, so it isn't connected to anything in this step; it's read as a bearing block positioned here and only joined when the main shaft threads through it in step 7. Worth Dennis checking the PDF for an arrow connecting fork-R that this crop doesn't show.
